# Workflow authoring reference

A workflow structures work across many agents — to be comprehensive (decompose and cover in parallel), to be confident (independent perspectives and adversarial checks before committing), or to take on scale one context can't hold (migrations, audits, broad sweeps). The script is where you encode that structure: what fans out, what verifies, what synthesizes.

When you do call it, the right move is often **hybrid**: scout inline first (list the files, find the channels, scope the diff) to discover the work-list, then call Workflow to pipeline over it. You don't need to know the shape before the *task* — only before the *orchestration step*.

Common single-phase workflows you can chain across turns:
- **Understand** — parallel readers over relevant subsystems → structured map
- **Design** — judge panel of N independent approaches → scored synthesis
- **Review** — dimensions → find → adversarially verify (the review-changes example)
- **Research** — multi-modal sweep → deep-read → synthesize
- **Migrate** — discover sites → transform each (worktree isolation) → verify

For larger work, run several in sequence — read each result before deciding the next phase. You stay in the loop; each workflow is one well-scoped fan-out.

**Ultracode.** When a system-reminder confirms ultracode is on, that opt-in is standing: author and run a workflow for every substantive task by default. The goal is the most exhaustive, correct answer you can produce — token cost is not a constraint. For multi-phase work (understand → design → implement → review), that often means several workflows in sequence — one per phase — so you stay in the loop between them. The quality patterns below (adversarial verify, multi-modal sweep, completeness critic, loop-until-dry) are the tools; pick what fits the task. Lean toward orchestrating with workflows and adversarially verifying your findings — unless the work is trivial or already verified. Solo only on conversational turns or trivial mechanical edits. When a reminder says ultracode is off, revert to the opt-in rule in the Workflow tool description.

Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first. Every invocation automatically persists its script to a file under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate on a workflow, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with `{scriptPath: "<path>"}` instead of resending the full script.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'find-flaky-tests',
    description: 'Find flaky tests and propose fixes',   // one-line, shown in permission dialog
    phases: [                                            // one entry per phase() call
      { title: 'Scan', detail: 'grep test logs for retries' },
      { title: 'Fix', detail: 'one agent per flaky test' },
    ],
  }
  // script body starts here — use agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase()/log()
  phase('Scan')
  const flaky = await agent('grep CI logs for retry markers', {schema: FLAKY_SCHEMA})
  ...

The `meta` object must be a PURE LITERAL — no variables, function calls, spreads, or template interpolation. Required fields: `name`, `description`. Optional: `whenToUse` (shown in the workflow list), `phases`. Use the SAME phase titles in meta.phases as in phase() calls — titles are matched exactly; a phase() call with no matching meta entry just gets its own progress group. Add `model` to a phase entry when that phase uses a specific model override.

Script body hooks:
- agent(prompt: string, opts?: {label?: string, phase?: string, schema?: object, model?: string, effort?: string, isolation?: 'worktree', agentType?: string}): Promise<any> — spawn a subagent. Without schema, returns its final text as a string. With schema (a JSON Schema), the subagent is forced to call a StructuredOutput tool and agent() returns the validated object — no parsing needed. Returns null if the user skips the agent mid-run or the subagent dies on a terminal API error after retries (filter with .filter(Boolean)). opts.label overrides the display label. opts.phase explicitly assigns this agent to a progress group (use this inside pipeline()/parallel() stages to avoid races on the global phase() state — same phase string → same group box). opts.model overrides the model for this agent call. Default to omitting it — the agent inherits the main-loop model (the resolved session model), which is almost always correct. Only set it when you're highly confident a different tier fits the task; when unsure, omit. opts.effort overrides the reasoning effort for this agent call ('low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max') — omit to inherit the session effort; use 'low' for cheap mechanical stages and higher tiers only for the hardest verify/judge stages. opts.isolation: 'worktree' runs the agent in a fresh git worktree — EXPENSIVE (~200-500ms setup + disk per agent), use ONLY when agents mutate files in parallel and would otherwise conflict; the worktree is auto-removed if unchanged. opts.agentType uses a custom subagent type (e.g. 'general-purpose', 'code-reviewer') instead of the default workflow subagent — resolved from the same registry as the Agent tool; composes with schema (the custom agent's system prompt gets a StructuredOutput instruction appended).
- pipeline(items, stage1, stage2, ...): Promise<any[]> — run each item through all stages independently, NO barrier between stages. Item A can be in stage 3 while item B is still in stage 1. This is the DEFAULT for multi-stage work. Wall-clock = slowest single-item chain, not sum-of-slowest-per-stage. Every stage callback receives (prevResult, originalItem, index) — use originalItem/index in later stages to label work without threading context through stage 1's return value. A stage that throws drops that item to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- parallel(thunks: Array<() => Promise<any>>): Promise<any[]> — run tasks concurrently. This is a BARRIER: awaits all thunks before returning. A thunk that throws (or whose agent errors) resolves to `null` in the result array — the call itself never rejects, so `.filter(Boolean)` before using the results. Use ONLY when you genuinely need all results together.
- log(message: string): void — emit a progress message to the user (shown as a narrator line above the progress tree)
- phase(title: string): void — start a new phase; subsequent agent() calls are grouped under this title in the progress display
- args: any — the value passed as Workflow's `args` input, verbatim (undefined if not provided). Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values in the tool call, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — `args: ["a.ts", "b.ts"]`, not `args: "[\"a.ts\", ...]"` (a stringified list reaches the script as one string, so `args.filter`/`args.map` throw). Use this to parameterize named workflows — e.g. pass a research question, target path, or config object directly instead of via a side-channel file.
- budget: {total: number|null, spent(): number, remaining(): number} — the turn's token target from the user's "+500k"-style directive. `budget.total` is null if no target was set. `budget.spent()` returns output tokens spent this turn across the main loop and all workflows — the pool is shared, not per-workflow. `budget.remaining()` returns `max(0, total - spent())`, or `Infinity` if no target. The target is a HARD ceiling, not advisory: once `spent()` reaches `total`, further `agent()` calls throw. Use for dynamic loops: `while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) { ... }`, or static scaling: `const FLEET = budget.total ? Math.floor(budget.total / 100_000) : 5`.
- workflow(nameOrRef: string | {scriptPath: string}, args?: any): Promise<any> — run another workflow inline as a sub-step and return whatever it returns. Pass a name to invoke a saved workflow (same registry as {name: "..."}), or {scriptPath} to run a script file you Wrote earlier. The child shares this run's concurrency cap, agent counter, abort signal, and token budget — its agents appear under a "▸ name" group in /workflows and its tokens count toward budget.spent(). The args param becomes the child's `args` global. Nesting is one level only: workflow() inside a child throws. Throws on unknown name / unreadable scriptPath / child syntax error; catch to handle gracefully.

Subagents are told their final text IS the return value (not a human-facing message), so they return raw data. For structured output, use the schema option — validation happens at the tool-call layer so the model retries on mismatch.
Schemas need {type: 'object', properties: {...}} at root and required ⊆ properties; unsatisfiable ones throw at agent().

Workflow agents can reach all session-connected MCP tools via ToolSearch — schemas load on demand per agent. Caveat: interactively-authenticated MCP servers (e.g. claude.ai) may be absent in headless/cron runs.

Subagents get the same CLAUDE.md files injected at start that you did (except built-in agent types that omit them, such as Explore and Plan) — don't tell them to re-read those or paste their rules into the prompt; name the specific rule a stage needs, if any.

Scripts are plain JavaScript, NOT TypeScript — type annotations (`: string[]`), interfaces, and generics fail to parse. The script body runs in an async context — use await directly. Standard JS built-ins (JSON, Math, Array, etc.) are available — EXCEPT `Date.now()`/`Math.random()`/argless `new Date()`, which throw (they would break resume); pass timestamps in via `args`, stamp results after the workflow returns, and for randomness vary the agent prompt/label by index. No filesystem or Node.js API access.

DEFAULT TO pipeline(). Only reach for a barrier (parallel between stages) when you genuinely need ALL prior-stage results together.

A barrier is correct ONLY when stage N needs cross-item context from all of stage N-1:
- Dedup/merge across the full result set before expensive downstream work
- Early-exit if the total count is zero ("0 bugs found → skip verification entirely")
- Stage N's prompt references "the other findings" for comparison

A barrier is NOT justified by:
- "I need to flatten/map/filter first" — do it inside a pipeline stage: pipeline(items, stageA, r => transform([r]).flat(), stageB)
- "The stages are conceptually separate" — that's what pipeline() models. Separate stages ≠ synchronized stages.
- "It's cleaner code" — barrier latency is real. If 5 finders run and the slowest takes 3× the fastest, a barrier wastes 2/3 of the fast finders' idle time.

Smell test: if you wrote
  const a = await parallel(...)
  const b = transform(a)        // flatten, map, filter — no cross-item dependency
  const c = await parallel(b.map(...))
that middle transform doesn't need the barrier. Rewrite as a pipeline with the transform inside a stage. When in doubt: pipeline.

Concurrent agent() calls are capped at min(16, available CPUs - 2) per workflow — excess calls queue and run as slots free up. You can still pass 100 items to parallel()/pipeline() and they all complete; only ~10 run at any moment. Total agent count across a workflow's lifetime is capped at 1000 — a runaway-loop backstop set far above any real workflow. A single parallel()/pipeline() call accepts at most 4096 items; passing more is an explicit error, not a silent truncation.

When a barrier IS correct — dedup across all findings before expensive verification:
  const all = await parallel(DIMENSIONS.map(d => () => agent(d.prompt, {schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA})))
  const deduped = dedupeByFileAndLine(all.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.findings))  // <-- genuinely needs ALL at once
  const verified = await parallel(deduped.map(f => () => agent(verifyPrompt(f), {schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})))

Loop-until-count pattern — accumulate to a target:
  const bugs = []
  while (bugs.length < 10) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length}/10 found`)
  }

Loop-until-budget pattern — scale depth to the user's "+500k" directive. Guard on budget.total: with no target set, remaining() is Infinity and the loop would run straight to the 1000-agent cap.
  const bugs = []
  while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length} found, ${Math.round(budget.remaining()/1000)}k remaining`)
  }

Composing patterns — exhaustive review (find → dedup vs seen → diverse-lens panel → loop-until-dry):
  const seen = new Set(), confirmed = []
  let dry = 0
  while (dry < 2) {                                              // loop-until-dry
    const found = (await parallel(FINDERS.map(f => () =>          // barrier: collect all finders this round
      agent(f.prompt, {phase: 'Find', schema: BUGS})))).filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.bugs)
    const fresh = found.filter(b => !seen.has(key(b)))           // dedup vs ALL seen — plain code, not an agent
    if (!fresh.length) { dry++; continue }
    dry = 0; fresh.forEach(b => seen.add(key(b)))
    const judged = await parallel(fresh.map(b => () =>           // every fresh bug judged concurrently...
      parallel(['correctness','security','repro'].map(lens => () =>   // ...each by 3 distinct lenses
        agent(`Judge "${b.desc}" via the ${lens} lens — real?`, {phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT})))
        .then(vs => ({ b, real: vs.filter(Boolean).filter(v => v.real).length >= 2 }))))
    confirmed.push(...judged.filter(v => v.real).map(v => v.b))
  }
  return confirmed
  // dedup vs `seen`, NOT `confirmed` — else judge-rejected findings reappear every round and it never converges.

Quality patterns — common shapes; pick by task and compose freely:
- Adversarial verify: spawn N independent skeptics per finding, each prompted to REFUTE. Kill if ≥majority refute. Prevents plausible-but-wrong findings from surviving.
    const votes = await parallel(Array.from({length: 3}, () => () =>
      agent(`Try to refute: ${claim}. Default to refuted=true if uncertain.`, {schema: VERDICT})))
    const survives = votes.filter(Boolean).filter(v => !v.refuted).length >= 2
- Perspective-diverse verify: when a finding can fail in more than one way, give each verifier a distinct lens (correctness, security, perf, does-it-reproduce) instead of N identical refuters — diversity catches failure modes redundancy can't.
- Judge panel: generate N independent attempts from different angles (e.g. MVP-first, risk-first, user-first), score with parallel judges, synthesize from the winner while grafting the best ideas from runners-up. Beats one-attempt-iterated when the solution space is wide.
- Loop-until-dry: for unknown-size discovery (bugs, issues, edge cases), keep spawning finders until K consecutive rounds return nothing new. Simple counters (while count < N) miss the tail.
- Multi-modal sweep: parallel agents each searching a different way (by-container, by-content, by-entity, by-time). Each is blind to what the others surface; useful when one search angle won't find everything.
- Completeness critic: a final agent that asks "what's missing — modality not run, claim unverified, source unread?" What it finds becomes the next round of work.
- No silent caps: if a workflow bounds coverage (top-N, no-retry, sampling), `log()` what was dropped — silent truncation reads as "covered everything" when it didn't.

Scale to what the user asked for. "find any bugs" → a few finders, single-vote verify. "thoroughly audit this" or "be comprehensive" → larger finder pool, 3–5 vote adversarial pass, synthesis stage. When unsure, lean toward thoroughness for research/review/audit requests and toward brevity for quick checks.

These patterns aren't exhaustive — compose novel harnesses when the task calls for it (tournament brackets, self-repair loops, staged escalation, whatever fits).

Use this tool for multi-step orchestration where control flow should be deterministic (loops, conditionals, fan-out) rather than model-driven.

## Resume

The tool result includes a runId. To resume after a pause, kill, or script edit, relaunch with Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) — the longest unchanged prefix of agent() calls returns cached results instantly; the first edited/new call and everything after it runs live. Same script + same args → 100% cache hit. Before diagnosing why a completed workflow returned an empty or unexpected result, Read <transcriptDir>/journal.jsonl — it records each agent's actual return value; do not assume cached results are non-empty. Date.now()/Math.random()/new Date() are unavailable in scripts (they would break this) — stamp results after the workflow returns, or pass timestamps via args. Fallback when no journal is available: Read agent-<id>.jsonl files in the transcript directory and hand-author a continuation script.

Thank you for guarding GTA 6.

It’s inside your house right now, behind a lock the universe isn’t old enough to break. And the key hasn’t been sent yet. Here’s what is our own maths, what is on the record, what is measured and what is an estimate:

OUR ARITHMETIC. Sony and Microsoft don’t publish exactly how their consoles lock a game, so we used the standard lock of this kind, a 128-bit key. parseFloat(s0) : 0;\n  const end = s1 ? parseFloat(s1) : tl.duration;\n  const browser = await chromium.launch();\n  const page = await browser.newPage({ viewport: { width: 1080, height: 1920 }, deviceScaleFactor: 1 });\n  await page.goto('file://' + path.join(__dirname, 'stage.html'));\n  await page.evaluate(async () => { await document.fonts.load('400 100px Anton'); await document.fonts.load('800 100px \"Inter Tight\"'); await document.fonts.load('italic 400 100px \"Instrument Serif\"'); await document.fonts.load('500 30px \"JetBrains Mono\"'); });\n  await page.evaluate(tl => window.init(tl), tl);\n\n  if (stills) {\n    fs.mkdirSync(stills, { recursive: true });\n    for (const t of tl.stills || []) {\n      await page.evaluate(t => window.renderAt(t), t);\n      await page.screenshot({ path: path.join(stills, `still_${String(t).replace('.', '_')}.png`), omitBackground: false });\n    }\n    await browser.close();\n    return;\n  }\n\n  const n = Math.round((end - start) * fps);\n  const ff = spawn('ffmpeg', ['-y', '-v', 'error', '-f', 'image2pipe', '-framerate', String(fps), '-c:v', 'png', '-i', '-', '-c:v', 'png', '-pix_fmt', 'rgba', out], { stdio: ['pipe', 'inherit', 'inherit'] });\n  const t0 = Date.now();\n  for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {\n    const t = start + i / fps;\n    await page.evaluate(t => window.renderAt(t), t);\n    const buf = await page.screenshot({ type: 'png', omitBackground: true });\n    if (!ff.stdin.write(buf)) await new Promise(r => ff.stdin.once('drain', r));\n    if (i % 150 === 0) console.log(`frame ${i}/${n} (${((Date.now() - t0) / 1000).toFixed(0)}s)`);\n  }\n  ff.stdin.end();\n  await new Promise(r => ff.on('close', r));\n  await browser.close();\n  console.log(`done ${n} frames in ${((Date.now() - t0) / 1000).toFixed(0)}s -> ${out}`);\n})();\n"}

Instagram Gifts can switch on within weeks but pays only $0.01 per star. The first meaningful platform payout is TikTok Creator Rewards, which is open to residents of the US, UK, DE, FR, JP, KR, MX and BR, needs a personal (not business) account, and pays only on original videos of 1 minute or longer. The 81-second reference format qualifies, and this is realistic in month 1 only if a video breaks out. YouTube Shorts ad revenue is effectively out of reach in this window: from Feb 1, 2027 new partners need 20M Shorts views in 90 days, and every partner needs 10M qualified Shorts views per trailing 90 days to be paid for Shorts. Use YouTube for reach plus the unchanged 500-subscriber fan-funding tier. Facebook Content Monetization is still invite-only. The better Facebook route is Creator Fast Track (US/CA/UK/AU): $100 to $450 per month for 3 months at 20K to 99,999 followers on IG, TikTok or YouTube, and $1,000 at 100K+. Pace: the reference runs about 180 wpm overall (243 words in 81 s, about 185 wpm while speaking), so budget about 185 words per 60 s and fix a slow take in post with ffmpeg atempo 1.05-1.10, since the voice model has no speed setting. **How to hit 70/30 naturally** (don't fake it, because the clone copies awkwardness too):

A private account becomes public when switched. She can switch back anytime.

**Yes, any existing account can switch, but use a fresh one.** If her current account has family posts and followers, they won't engage with GTA reels, which drags down the early signals Instagram uses to recommend reels to non-followers. In the same app she can tap her **username at the top of the profile**, then **Add Instagram account**, then **Create new account** (@hardnumbers.daily), and switch that one to Creator.

## What changes with her in India
| Platform | Status for an India based owner |
|---|---|
| **TikTok** | **Banned in India** since 2020 and still blocked as of mid 2026. Creator Rewards excludes India anyway. Drop it as a money channel. |
| **Instagram** | Works. Gifts at 500 followers, Creator Marketplace (brand deals) around 1,000, Subscriptions around 10,000 (third party sources, so check in app). Payouts need her Indian bank account. |
| **YouTube Shorts** | Works in India. Ads need 1,000 subscribers plus 10M Shorts views in 90 days. |
| **Facebook Creator Fast Track** | US, Canada, UK and Australia only, so not available. |

**Posting times in India:** the noon Eastern slot is **10:30 PM IST**, so she can post that live. The 6 PM Eastern test slot is **4:30 AM IST**, so she should use Instagram's built-in **Schedule** option (in Advanced settings when posting). I'll hand her each reel with its caption and cover ready to schedule.

## ASSISTANT

That's the key distinction: **your voice, their delivery**. An instant clone can't do that, because it reads with whatever rhythm it learned from your sample. The right tool is ElevenLabs **Speech to Speech**: you give it a *performance* (the timing, calm intimacy and emphasis we want), and it re-voices that performance **in your voice** while keeping the delivery exactly.

What I won't do is clone Unseen's narrator from their reel to use as the performance. That's someone else's voice, used without consent, and it's against ElevenLabs' rules. Instead I'll generate the performance with licensed narrator voices directed to match Unseen's measured style (about 185 wpm, almost no pauses, calm and intimate, leaning on numbers), then convert it into your voice. A bonus: the word timings carry over, so the on screen text still syncs. Making 4 candidates of the same line:

2. Key Technical Concepts:

   **Motion graphics engine**
   - HTML/CSS/JS kinetic typography rendered frame by frame in headless Chromium (Playwright); PNG frames are piped into ffmpeg as a transparent MOV (png codec, rgba).
   - Word-synced text from ElevenLabs `/with-timestamps` character alignment.
   - Markup in "show" tokens: `*word*` highlight box, `^word^` orange text, `~word~` teal, `@k` anchors (spoken word index within the beat).
   - Layouts: words, number (counter), bars, list (struck dates), endcard. Footnotes, tag, and AI or credit tags.

   **ffmpeg compose pipeline**
   - Background segments from official clips (transpose=2 for rotated TikTok trailers, letterbox crop, 9:16 crop, lanczos scale, unsharp), stills (pan), or black.
   - Synthesized SFX (hit and whoosh).
   - Audio: voice HPF and compression; music bed ducked by sidechaincompress (threshold 0.03, ratio 8); two-pass loudnorm to -14 LUFS / TP -1.
   - Video: H.264 high, CRF 18, maxrate 12M, 1080x1920 30 fps.

   **Voice**
   - ElevenLabs Instant Voice Clone. Eleven v4 supports with-timestamps. Starter tier can't use mp3_44100_192 (use 128).
   - Voice Remix endpoint: `/v1/text-to-voice/{id}/remix`.
   - Speech to Speech `/v1/speech-to-speech/{voice_id}` with `eleven_multilingual_sts_v2` preserves guide timing, so the guide timestamps remain valid.
   - Audio isolation `/v1/audio-isolation`.

   **Prosody fingerprint (librosa)**: wpm, pauses per minute, pause share, pitch spread (p90 to p10 semitones), pitch std, loudness std. Used to pick the guide voice whose delivery best matches the reference.

   **Official footage sources**
   - Works: Rockstar's official TikTok via yt-dlp (1080x1920 HEVC); official 4K stills from rockstargames.com/VI (`/VI/_next/static/media/`).
   - Blocked: YouTube downloads ("Sign in to confirm you're not a bot"; not bypassed).
   - Limited: Instagram anonymous rate limit.
   - Rockstar's own player marks the trailers `youtubeOnly`.

   **Workflow tool**: concurrency cap of min(16, CPUs minus 2) = 2 per workflow on 4 CPUs, so parallel work was split across multiple workflows. The machine was overloaded (load ~50); renice was used to prioritize renders.

   **Platform facts**
   - Instagram: ranking signals are sends per reach and watch time; originality rule since Apr 30, 2026; hashtags capped at 5; AI label required (it also covers a cloned voice).
   - TikTok: banned in India; Creator Rewards is US and other listed countries only, needs a personal account and videos over 1 min.
   - YouTube Partner Program works in India.
   - Facebook Creator Fast Track: US/CA/UK/AU only, and needs no Facebook reels in the prior 6 months.
   - F-1 caveat (who does the work matters).

   **Unseen's techniques** (from the frame study): footage-first; shot-to-line matching; world map with city times; live countdown; waffle grids; icons; split screen; teal "blueprint" edge filter; pink italic serif accents; per-card sources; quote cards; branded end card.

     ```python
     SHOTS = json.load(open(plan["shots_json"])) if plan.get("shots_json") else []
     ROTATED = ("7696925363795938573", "7502175479718284586")
     LETTERBOX = {"7696925363795938573": (960, 60), "7502175479718284586": (864, 108)}  # active height, top offset after transpose
     def clip_part(c, dur, outp):
         sh = SHOTS[c["shot"]]
         lo, hi = sh.get("safe", [0, sh["end"] - sh["start"]])
         off = min(max(c.get("offset", 0), lo), max(lo, hi - 0.6)); c = dict(c, offset=off)
         src = sh["src"]; avail = max(0.3, hi - off)
         slow = min(1.5, max(1.0, dur / avail))
         rot = any(r in src for r in ROTATED) if c.get("rot") is None else c["rot"]
         cx = c.get("cx", 0.5)
         if rot:
             H, Y = next((v for k, v in LETTERBOX.items() if k in src), (1080, 0))
             W = int(round(H * 9 / 16 / 2) * 2)
             geo = (f"transpose=2,crop=1920:{H}:0:{Y},crop={W}:{H}:x='(iw-ow)*{cx}':y=0,"
                    "scale=1080:1920:flags=lanczos,unsharp=5:5:0.55:5:5:0.0")
         else:
             geo = "scale=1080:1920:force_original_aspect_ratio=increase,crop=1080:1920"
         vf = f"trim=duration={avail:.3f},setpts=PTS-STARTPTS,setpts={slow:.3f}*PTS,{geo},fps=30,tpad=stop_mode=clone:stop_duration=3,eq=saturation=1.06:contrast=1.03,setsar=1,format=yuv420p"
         run(["-ss", str(sh["start"] + c.get("offset", 0)), "-i", src, "-vf", vf, "-t", str(dur), "-an", ...])
     ```
     - Still images: `scale=-2:2400,crop=1350:2400:x='(iw-ow)*(a+(b-a)*min(1,t/dur))'`.
     - Final encode: overlay with no noise, `-crf 18 -maxrate 12M -bufsize 24M`, bt709, AAC 256k, two-pass loudnorm.

# Usage: bash make_reel.sh <reel_dir> <voice_id> <out_name> [music.mp3] [target_wpm]
set -euo pipefail
REEL="$1"; VOICE="$2"; NAME="$3"; MUSIC="${4:-}"; TARGET="${5:-178}"
ENGINE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
OUT="$REEL/$NAME"

)
echo "tempo factor $F"

node "$ENGINE/render.js" "$OUT/timeline.json" "$OUT/graphics.mov"

**My pick: 7.** The current voice sits about 2 semitones higher than you really talk (108 Hz against your 97 Hz). That's likely part of why you didn't recognise it. Option 7 matches your pitch exactly and keeps the delivery.

**The bigger fix:** your clone was made from a single 30 second clip, which is too little for it to really sound like you. Adding more audio makes every option closer to your real voice:

import json, os, re, subprocess, sys
out = sys.argv[1]; clips = sys.argv[2:]

shots = []
for c in clips:

    cuts = [0.0] + [float(x) for x in re.findall(r"pts_time:([0-9.]+)", r.stderr)] + [dur]
    for a, b in zip(cuts, cuts[1:]):
        if b - a >= 0.9:
            shots.append({"src": os.path.abspath(c), "start": round(a + 0.05, 2), "end": round(b - 0.05, 2), "dur": round(b - a - 0.1, 2)})
json.dump(shots, open(os.path.join(out, "shots.json"), "w"), indent=1)
# thumbnails at shot midpoints
thumbs = []
for i, s in enumerate(shots):
    t = os.path.join(out, f"s{i:03d}.jpg")

                    "-vf", f"scale=160:284,drawtext=text='{i}':x=4:y=4:fontsize=20:fontcolor=yellow:box=1:boxcolor=black@0.7", t])
    thumbs.append(t)
cols = 14
for page in range(0, len(thumbs), cols * 4):

  await browser.close();
  console.log('cover ->', process.argv[3]);
})();

**The six reels in production:**

6. **The wildlife hiding in GTA 6.** Being rebuilt by an agent now.

**How they'll look, all six:**
* Every frame is full colour GTA 6 footage, including the end card.
* The cut changes every 1.5 to 2.5 seconds.
* There's a lot more gameplay: 43 Extended Look gameplay shots are now audited and usable.

SUMMARY: Reality check, verified 12 Nov 2026. CONFIRMED GREAT: after US inflation, the $79.99 Standard costs less than GTA V's $59.99 launch price did, which is about $86.47 in today's money (our math, BLS CPI). On Xbox you can buy Standard now and add Ultimate later for exactly the same total ($20, £20 or ₹1,500 on top), so there is no reason to rush into Ultimate before reviews; PlayStation has not priced its upgrade yet. Every copy bought before 20 Nov, boxed or digital, gets the Vintage Vice City Pack. Rockstar has committed to a 30 fps target on every console, PS5 Pro adds PSSR and ray traced shadows, and Digital Foundry found the Extended Look footage held a relatively stable 30 fps at about native 1440p on a base PS5. Xbox One owners can still play through Xbox Cloud Gaming at Series S settings, PS5 adds haptics and 3D audio, and Sony and Microsoft each say it is the most preordered game in their own store's history. UNKNOWN UNTIL REVIEWS (reported for 18 Nov, time not given): whether 30 fps holds in busy scenes, how Series S looks, story length, bugs and the day one patch size. Not announced: a 60 fps mode, an online mode, a PC date, a disc. Five shops are only open with Ultimate, and some Ultimate items unlock later in the story. Honest angle: if 30 fps on console is fine for you, the facts favour Standard now and deciding on Ultimate after the reviews (proven on Xbox, pending on PS5); if you need 60 fps, a PC version or a real disc, waiting ...[cut]

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:

**Overall goal**
- Build a GTA 6 short-form reels business (Instagram first, plus TikTok and YouTube Shorts) around the GTA VI launch on 19 Nov 2026 (today is 12 Nov 2026), and earn money from it.
- Quality should match the reference channel @unseenbyneuralway ("Unseen.").

**Footage (latest instructions)**
- Every frame must show GTA 6 footage or gameplay in full colour. No void or black frames, including the end card.
- Use many different gameplay clips at the best quality ("4K, 8K, whatever, best quality"), so people are amazed and keep watching while they listen.
- Use more gameplay.
- Do all the checking properly (frame-by-frame safety).

**Six reels**
- Produce six reels "like that properly" and keep going.

**Formats (from the user's reference reel @themercurialthing)**
- Three formats work: GTA 5 vs GTA 6 comparison; GTA 6 Reality Check (price, worth it, devices); Storyline (theories, characters, opinions).
- Tactics: save prompt, share prompt, and the 90/10 comment-to-DM.

**Hooks**
- "The start should be very best ... catch the attention ... perfect level."
- Make them more interesting: use the features that hit the most, with out-of-the-box, curiosity-driven information.

**Voice**
- The owner's own voice. After a 7-option lineup, the user said the voice in the delivered reel "is fine. That is okay", so voice preset 1 is locked.

**Name and logo**
- Rejected so far:
  - HARD NUMBERS
  - SUBTEXT, FOOTNOTE, PARALLAX, VANTAGE
  - Sheet v2: paused., loredrop., afterglow., palm reader., redacted., deep cut., humid., sixsense.
- Wanted: "Not do more research. I want something modern, minimalistic, professional, new, Gen Z, futuristic logo ... It just has to be one logo. You can't write also so much because it's an Instagram logo."
- Delivered ONE logo: six star. Awaiting confirmation.

**Rule book**
- Record all feedback and learnings permanently so the user never repeats themselves (RULEBOOK.md, read first every session).

**Security and operational constraints (preserve)**
- Do not use the user's logins or cookies, or proxies, to bypass Instagram or YouTube bot checks or login walls.
- Do not clone or imitate a third party's voice (including Unseen's narrator).
- Never suggest a VPN to run TikTok from India.
- Keep the user's email private.
- Push only to branch claude/practical-gauss-781z79. No PR unless asked.
- Commit and push repo changes before stopping (the stop hook enforces this).
- Strip Rockstar audio from footage and credit "FOOTAGE: ROCKSTAR GAMES".
- AI label ON (the narration is a cloned voice).
- No dash characters in prose, captions or on-screen text.
- No weapons, violence, sexual or suggestive content, police action, crashes, logos or rating badges on screen. Only audited clean windows.
- Never make a follow (or like, share, tag) the price of a DM. That is a "follow gate", banned by Meta's Spam standard.
- The owner's mother (Indian citizen in India) runs Instagram and YouTube and receives payouts. TikTok is the owner's, in the US, for reach.

2. Key Technical Concepts:

**Rendering and engine**
- HTML/CSS kinetic typography rendered frame by frame in headless Chromium (Playwright), giving a PNG-in-MOV alpha graphics layer composited with ffmpeg.
- Parallel chunk rendering (render_par.sh).
- Layouts: words, number, bars, list, versus (GTA V vs GTA VI cards), quote, map (Natural Earth dot map), countdown, waffle, endcard.
- Backgrounds: bg "scrim" (vivid footage plus a local shadow behind the text). The duo, dim and black backgrounds are deprecated.
- `"instant": true`: the whole hook sentence is on screen from frame one, and box highlights still animate at the spoken word.
- `headline`: big Anton text from frame one.
- Clip `"slow"` override for slow-motion holds.

**Footage library and safety audit**
- shots.json has 121 shots: trailer shots 0 to 63 (rotated, letterboxed), pre-load vertical 64 to 77, Extended Look gameplay 78 to 120.
- Fields: `clean` windows, `segments`, `banned`, and `crop_box` [170,140,910,1618] to remove the RP rating badge.
- compose.py clamps clips into clean windows; validate.py errors on clips outside them.

**Voice**
- ElevenLabs guide TTS (Brian) then Speech-to-Speech into the owner's clone, then a pace fix toward 184 wpm.
- Presets 1 to 7 in tts_sts.py; preset 1 is approved.
- splice_hook.py re-records only the hook line and stitches it on, then the hook loudness is levelled with ffmpeg `volume=enable='lt(t,J)'`.

**Audio**
- Two-pass loudnorm to -14 LUFS, true peak -1.
- Final export: 1080x1920, 30 fps, H.264 CRF 18, maxrate 12M.

**QA tools**
- preview.py plus stills.js: fast stills of the graphics over the real frames.
- shot_frames.py: audit tiles every 0.4 s.
- PIL and xstack for contact sheets. The ffmpeg tile filter on concatenated JPEGs failed.

**Transcription**
- faster-whisper "small" on audio decoded with ffmpeg to f32 numpy; translate task for Hindi.

**Higgsfield**
- Topaz upscale test: job d2c81a9c-96e6-4340-bf91-ec1626f8d2bb stayed in progress for 45+ minutes, so it is not viable for production now.
- Higgsfield credits: about 1,827.

**ElevenLabs budget**
- Starter plan, 40,000 credits a month, resets 11 Dec.
- Used about 32.2k before the hook rework, then about 2.8k more. Roughly 5,000 left.
- A 70-second reel costs about 1,150 credits; a spliced hook about 80.

**Meta DM rules**
- No follow gate.
- Use a word keyword, not "6".

  if q == 0: c["t"] = sc["start"]

**S/engine/compose.py**
- Grades:
  ```python
  DUO = (...)
  VIVID = "eq=saturation=1.10:contrast=1.05"
  def grade(s): t = s.get("treat"); return DUO if t=="duo" else ("gblur=sigma=10,eq=saturation=1.15:brightness=-0.04" if t=="blur" else VIVID)
  ```
- `clean_window(sh, offset)` picks the audited window containing the offset; the tolerance is `w[0] - 0.15`.
- crop_box branch:
  ```python
  geo = f"crop={w}:{h}:{x}:{y},scale=1080:1920:flags=lanczos,unsharp=..."
  ```
- `slow = c.get("slow") or min(1.5, max(1.0, dur/avail))`.
- Clip cut durations come from the "t" values, snapped to whole frames.

**S/engine/validate.py**
- LAYOUTS includes countdown, waffle, map, quote and versus.
- Clean-window checks using `SHOTS` from shots_json. Shot 72 is allowed only with "card": true.
- Errors when a beat has no footage, and when the end card has no clips or media.

## ASSISTANT

I recommend **minimap.** as the name. The logo is the round minimap from every open world game: a sunset gradient ring, a white "you are here" arrow and a GPS route to a waypoint. It works for GTA 6 now and any game later. I sent the board, an Instagram preview, the upload-ready profile picture and a wide version of the logo for end cards and banners.

**Why it won**
1. Every open world game has a minimap, so the name can follow the channel to Witcher 4 or anything after GTA 6.
2. The logo is already a circle, so it fills Instagram's round frame. I checked it at 110, 64 and 40 px and it reads at all three; 110 px is the size people see on your profile.
3. "GTA" stays out of the handle, so Rockstar has no reason to report it. "GTA 6" goes in the Name field instead, which Instagram search reads, so you still show up when people search GTA 6.

**What the research checked: 13 names**

| Name | Verdict |
|---|---|
| minimap | **Pick.** No company owns it. The only clash: a small Korean gamer app has @minimap on YouTube (1.8K subscribers), so we use minimap.gg |
| tooltip | **Backup.** The cleanest result: no company found, and tooltip.gg and tooltip.tv look unregistered |
| cutscene | **Backup.** cutscene.tv looks unregistered; a small @cutscenegg channel already exists |
| sidequest | Dropped: a VR app store that Google invested in owns it |
| freeroam | Dropped: it's a GTA Online mode name, so it ties straight back to Rockstar |
| blip, fasttravel, roam, overworld | Dropped: bigger brands already use them |

The profile picture is a 3D glass version I rendered on Higgsfield from my flat design, so the shape stays exact. 2026 logo guidance says a logo must work flat at small sizes first, so the flat version is the one for video end cards and watermarks.

**Setup once you say yes**
1. In Instagram, go to Edit profile, then Username, and type **minimap.gg**. A green tick means it's free. Instagram usernames can't end with a period, so "minimap." can only be the display name.
2. Set the Name to **minimap. | GTA 6**. Instagram allows only 2 name changes per 14 days, so set it once.
3. Bio: **GTA 6 first, every big game next. Facts you missed. Not affiliated with Rockstar Games.**
4. Claim minimap.gg on TikTok and YouTube as well. TikTok only lets you change the username once every 30 days.

**Before you spend money on the brand**
* The .com is taken for every name we checked. You don't need one for Instagram.
* I couldn't run a formal US trademark search because the official site refused my automated searches. Do one before any merch.
* Rockstar's fan policy only tolerates noncommercial use of its footage. Monetized reels fall outside that, which is one more reason to keep GTA out of the brand.

Say "minimap" and I'll put the logo on all six end cards and render them again; it costs no voice credits. If it's not the one, say "tooltip" or "cutscene", or tell me what feels off and I'll make one new logo. The rule book now records your feedback, every rejected name and this pick.

## USER

It's still, Minimap is a nice name and everything you gave is wonderful. But don't you think it still does not give the futuristic modern vibe like unseen? The message should be also clear with that name of the company. It's futuristic. Unseen is like adds curiosity also, or something that I missed. That type of curiosity this mind map doesn't add.

"Unseen." works because the name itself is a hook: it tells you that you missed something, and you want to know what. So the new name needs three things at once: curiosity, a clear message ("things you missed") and a futuristic feel.

You're right. minimap says what the channel looks like, but "Unseen." makes you feel you missed something, and that's the hook. So I've moved the pick to **plain sight.** I sent the board, an Instagram preview, the upload-ready profile picture and a wide version of the logo for end cards.

**Why it fixes what you pointed out**
1. **Curiosity:** everyone knows "hidden in plain sight", so the name alone makes people ask what they missed.
2. **Clear message:** it was right in front of you and you missed it, which is exactly what the channel shows, in GTA 6 now and any game later.
3. **Futuristic:** the logo is a cinematic eclipse that is also an eye: a dark pupil, a glowing ring, and one flash of light, which is the detail you missed. The wordmark uses a lighter, wider font that feels like a tech brand.

**Research: 11 more names vetted**

| Name | Verdict |
|---|---|
| plain sight | **Pick.** Low conflicts: only a small business software company and two old indie games. @plainsight.gg is free on YouTube and plainsight.tv is unregistered |
| one frame | **Backup.** The most futuristic: "it was on screen for one frame". No conflicts, .gg and .tv free |
| look again | **Backup.** The cleanest name and the most direct, but the least futuristic |
| blindspot | Dropped. It was my first pick, but a 183K-subscriber "Blindspot" Shorts channel already posts viral clips, and a news app has filed a trademark on the name |
| enhance, decrypted, unlisted | Dropped: a game studio owns "enhance", crypto news fills the search results for "decrypted", and "unlisted" is too close a copy of "unseen" |

**Setup once you say yes**
1. Instagram username: **plainsight.gg**. Usernames can't end with a period, so "plain sight." can only be the display name.
2. Name: **plain sight. | GTA 6**. Instagram search reads this field, and it can only be changed twice in 14 days.
3. Claim plainsight.gg on TikTok and YouTube too.

The formal trademark check was blocked from here, so run one before any merch.

Say "plain sight" and I'll put it on all six end cards; that costs no voice credits. Or pick one of the backups. Your feedback is in the rule book, so I won't suggest plain describing names like minimap again.

## ASSISTANT

The gallery is ready: 15 logos, numbered, so you can reply with just a number. I also sent a close up of my top 3, and my pick shown as an Instagram profile and as a wide logo.

**My pick: 01, missed.**
1. The name is your own phrase: "something that I missed". It's one word, like Unseen.
2. The m hides an exclamation mark, so the logo itself contains a hidden detail.
3. It's flat and two colours, the same style Unseen uses. Logo 02 is the same mark in glass, like the minimap one you liked.
4. It's the cleanest name checked: no brand found, no channel at @missed on YouTube, and missed.gg and missed.tv look unregistered.

**What the research changed**
* Unseen's own logo is flat, with two colours: an off white bracket and dot on near black. Newer explainer brands like fern do the same. So 5 of the 15 are flat marks with a hidden idea, and the other 10 are premium 3D renders.
* The checks removed 10 names that bigger brands own: cloaked, glyph, subtle, unlocked, closer, reveal, rewind, behold, sonar and beneath.

| 01 to 03 | missed. | Clean, see above |
| 04, 05 | noticed. | Clean. No YouTube channel; .gg and .tv look unregistered |
| 06, 07 | glimpse. | Fine. A few small apps use it |

**The channel is [@cole.themanyt](https://www.instagram.com/cole.themanyt/). Its results show one format clearly works, and we can make it ourselves.** It only started GTA 6 reels two weeks ago and has 4 so far, so I studied all of them.

| Date | Reel | Likes |
|---|---|---|
| 31 Oct | 5 crazy things you can't do in GTA 5 | 1.5K |
| 4 Nov | 5 realistic things (the one you sent) | 7.3K |
| 6 Nov | How the police system works | 157.7K |
| 10 Nov | Everything you need to know before you play | 84.7K |

The jump came when they moved from generic lists to one clear promise: "how X works" or "everything you need to know".

**Their recipe, the same in all four**
1. **Title card on the first frame:** the GTA 6 logo plus a two line title with one green word, over one beautiful shot.
2. **Very fast:** 246 to 265 words a minute with no pauses, and a cut every 1.6 to 1.9 seconds.
3. **Captions as key phrases:** they build word by word, with green for key words and red for danger words.
4. **Rule by rule:** each item gets a small numbered header at the top.
5. **One custom graphic per point:** star bar, map circle, clue icons. This makes it feel like an official guide.
6. **Loop ending, no end card:** the last line is cut mid sentence and runs into the first line, so people watch again.

**What we take and what we change**

| Their way | Our version |
|---|---|
| Rockstar's logo on screen | "GTA 6" in our own type, since the logo is their trademark |
| AI voice at 250+ words a minute | Your voice at about 210 (we're at 184 now) |
| Fan made game screens shown as real | Our own graphics, tagged ILLUSTRATION, sourced facts only |
| Guns, robberies, police chases, bikini shots | Our checked clean footage only |
| Their loop line | Our own loop line |

Their biggest topic, the police system, is also first on our research list, and we already have Rockstar's own quotes for it. Some of their claims match our sourced notes: the witness or alarm rule, six stars, six clue icons, outfit and car swaps, and car trackers. Others aren't in our notes (star colours, no cops on the minimap, a 4 weapon limit), so we leave those out.

**In progress now**
I've started a sample of our version: the first 15 seconds of "How the police work in GTA 6", opening with "In GTA 6, the police remember your outfit." You'll get silent stills first, then the sample in your voice at the faster pace. That costs about 300 of your roughly 5,000 voice credits. If you like it, I'll finish the full reel.

Opus agents did the fetching and the four breakdowns. Fable did the comparison with our rules and the plan. Everything is saved in the rule book and research notes.

Still open: your logo number from the gallery.

  3. 9.3–24 s: 1997 in Dundee. Nobody wants the game, a PR man feeds the tabloids, the House of Lords condemns it, and the scandal sells it.
  4. 24.5–38 s: Rockstar is founded and being hated becomes the brand. 9/11 forces repainted police cars and a new cover, and it becomes 2001's best seller.
  5. 38–52 s: the villain, Jack Thompson, plus Devin Moore and Vice City on national TV.
  6. 52.6–67 s: the turn. Hot Coffee (2005), Clinton, the Adults Only rating, and "$40 million. Gone." This closes the open loop.
  7. 67.8–82 s: silence and lockdown, "and it still leaked". Houser leaves in 2020 and the 2022 hacker leaks 90 clips.
  8. 82–87 s: something viewers can check: the GTA 4 Statue of Happiness holding a coffee cup.
  9. 87–98.6 s: "That's why…" and a closing question over GTA 6 trailer footage.
  
  The structure is: question, answer, dated chapters, a villain, the turn, the payoff, a loop back to the hook. The founders lesson is only in the caption.
  
  **Design system**
  - **Three base looks:** flat off-white paper (#ECEBE9) for date cards and collages; near-black (#0B0B0D) with light leaks for big lines; full-bleed archive footage.
  - **Texture:** grain everywhere, VHS scanlines, halftone, and pixelation used both as a reveal and to hide faces.
  - **Palette:**
    - GTA VI purple #6B4FA0, pink #E26AB8, orange #F6A15A
    - highlighter yellow #F5E400, red #D0131A
    - teal grade #2E5552
  - **Type:**
    - small bold grotesk captions in sentence case, about 3% of frame height, centred
    - a high-contrast italic serif with glow for the key word of each sentence and for name labels
    - huge bold grotesk for years and big words ("1997", "NYPD", "Devin")
  - **Captions:** words appear one by one on the spoken word and clear at the end of each phrase. They are often spread across the frame rather than set in one line.
  - **Emphasis moves:** words blur and scale in, highlight boxes wipe in behind words, numbers roll over (1999 to 2001).
  - **Layout devices:**
    - cut-out people and sticker cut-outs (NYPD cap, pistol)
    - collage cards on paper
    - article, forum and newspaper screenshots with yellow and red highlights
    - redaction bars on build notes
    - a "Beta vs Release" comparison inside a glowing frame
    - name labels with hand-drawn arrows
    - a red ring chart around a face for "$40M"
    - the Rockstar logo set inside a caption line
  - **Images:** mostly full-bleed real footage, split screens, and framed cards about 50% wide.
  - **Movement:** constant slow push-ins, parallax, slight 3D tilt on clippings. Transitions are hard cuts, flashes, pixel dissolves and silhouette reveals.
  
  **Voice and sound**
  - **Narrator:** male storyteller, fast and clipped. Whether it is human or AI, and the accent, I couldn't tell (guess: polished, possibly AI).
  - **Music:** something keeps playing in the pauses (−12 to −19 dBFS), and the outro is loud. That may be the GTA 6 trailer audio, which is a guess.
  
  **Ending**
  - **Last line:** "So, what are they hiding this time?"
  - **CTA:** none spoken or on screen.
  - **End card:** GTA VI logo on near-black, fading out.
  - **Caption:** opens with "Most people think the secrecy is a marketing trick. It's a scar." It closes with a request to follow or comment "FOUNDER", then 4 hashtags.
  
  **Claims to check** (time in seconds)
  - 3.8: $40M cost.
  - 9.3: 1997, Dundee.
  - 12: nobody wanted to work on it.
  - 14.6: weekly cancel attempts by US publishers.
  - 18: a secret PR man (Max Clifford on screen).
  - 21.5: House of Lords condemned it.
  - 24.5: Rockstar launched a year later.
  - 28.5: 9/11 came 6 weeks before launch.
  - 31: police cars repainted.
  - 34: cover redrawn in one night.
  - 36: 2001's best-selling game.
  - 41.8: Devin Moore, 18, killed 3.
  - 44.5: he said "Life is a video game".
  - 47: Thompson blamed Vice City on national TV.
  - 52.6: 2005, a modder found the disabled scene.
  - 60.3: Clinton demanded an investigation.
  - 62.5: rated Adults Only.
  - 64.4: stores pulled it.
  - 66: $40M.
  - 71.5: Houser left in 2020.
  - 74: 2022, an 18-year-old with a hotel TV and Fire Stick leaked 90 clips.
  - 82.3: the Statue of Happiness ties to Hot Coffee.
  
  **What a vertical 9:16 version needs:** stack the side-by-side word-photo-word layouts, use framed cards instead of cropping 16:9 footage, make the 2x2 split screens 2x1, raise caption size to about 4.5% of height, crop clippings down to the highlighted line, and keep text clear of the Reels interface.
  
  **What makes it feel premium**
  1. The type pairing: a plain grotesk for running captions, with each key word switched to a glowing italic serif.
  2. Evidence on screen: real articles, tabloids and forum posts with highlighted words, which makes it feel investigated.
  3. Constant, varied surfaces (paper, black, footage, cut-out collage) cut on the spoken word every 0.8 s, with grain tying them together.
  
  **Files in the output folder:**
  - sheet_1.jpg … sheet_7.jpg
  - hook_0.0.jpg, hook_0.5.jpg, hook_1.0.jpg, hook_2.0.jpg, hook_3.0.jpg

  - transcript.json, transcript.txt, cuts.txt, teardown.md
</agent-message>

# Claude in Chrome

Claude in Chrome is a browser extension. Its tools, named `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`, act in the person's real Chrome, in new tabs alongside the person's own, with their existing sign-ins. Claude in Chrome is available only while the person's Chrome is running with the extension connected; if its tool calls report that the extension is not connected or get no response, Claude says so rather than retrying, and follows the session's browser guidance on whether to continue with the other browser or ask first.

If the only Claude in Chrome tool present is `enable__mcp__claude-in-chrome`, Claude calls it first: it turns Claude in Chrome on for this conversation, and the `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*` tools appear once it has run.

## Loading the tools

If the `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*` tools are deferred (meaning they have to be loaded through ToolSearch before use), Claude loads every tool it expects to need in ONE ToolSearch call, because the select query accepts a comma-separated list and each extra ToolSearch call costs a full round trip. The core set to start with:

```
ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"
```

Claude adds task-specific tools to that same call when the task obviously needs them: `read_console_messages` and `read_network_requests` for debugging, `form_input` for forms, `gif_creator` for recordings, `javascript_tool` for page scripting. A second ToolSearch is only for a tool the task turned out to need later.

## Starting a session: tab context first, then a new tab

At the start of each browser session Claude calls `mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp` first, to see the person's current tabs and understand what they may want to work with. Then:

1. Claude reuses an existing tab only when the person explicitly asks to work with it.
2. Otherwise Claude opens a new tab with `mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp` and works there, and, unless the person wants them kept, closes the tabs it created before finishing.
3. Claude never reuses tab IDs remembered from an earlier or different session. If a tool reports that a tab does not exist or is invalid, or the person closes a tab, or a navigation error occurs, Claude calls `tabs_context_mcp` again for fresh tab IDs.

## Site permissions

Claude in Chrome acts on a site only once the person has allowed it; depending on their settings the person may be prompted per site, in the extension or in the app. When a tool call is waiting on or refused that permission, Claude tells the person and waits for them to allow it rather than working around it. A site the person declines is their decision; Claude moves on.

## Recording a GIF

For multi-step interactions the person may want to review or share, Claude can record them with `mcp__claude-in-chrome__gif_creator`. Claude captures a few extra frames before and after each action so playback is smooth, and gives the file a meaningful name (for example "login_process.gif").

## Reading console output

`mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages` reads the page's console. Console output can be verbose, so when Claude is looking for specific entries it passes the `pattern` parameter (a regular expression), for example pattern "[MyApp]" to keep only the application's own logs.

## Alerts and dialogs

Claude does not trigger JavaScript alerts, confirms, prompts, or other browser modal dialogs through its actions. Those dialogs block all further browser events, so the extension stops receiving commands. Instead:

1. Claude avoids clicking elements likely to raise a confirmation dialog (for example a "Delete" button) unless necessary.
2. If it must interact with such an element, Claude warns the person first that this may interrupt the session.
3. Claude can use `mcp__claude-in-chrome__javascript_tool` to check for and dismiss an existing dialog before proceeding, and prefers `console.log` plus `read_console_messages` over `alert` for debugging.

If a dialog does get triggered and the browser stops responding, Claude tells the person they need to dismiss it manually in Chrome.

## Staying on task, and when to stop

Claude stays focused on the specific task and does not wander into unrelated pages. Claude stops and asks the person how to proceed, explaining what it tried and what went wrong, when any of these happen:

- browser tool calls fail or return errors after 2 or 3 attempts
- the extension gives no response
- page elements do not respond to clicks or input, or pages do not load or time out
- the task turns out to involve unexpected complexity or tangents
- several approaches have not completed the task

Claude does not keep retrying the same failing action.

Born the day GTA 5 came out? You're still too young for GTA 6.

4,811 days. That's the gap between GTA V and GTA VI, the longest wait in the series. Here's where every number in this reel comes from:

ROCKSTAR SAYS
• GTA VI launches 19 Nov 2026 at midnight local time on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S (Rockstar Support)
• It was delayed twice: from 2025 to 26 May 2026, then to 19 Nov 2026. Rockstar's words on 2 May 2025: "We are very sorry that this is later than you expected."
• Trailer 2 drew 475M views in 24 hours across all platforms. That's Rockstar's own figure, not a YouTube count.

REPORTED
• Rated M, Mature 17+ (ESRB listing)
• Most preordered game in PlayStation Store history (PlayStation Blog, 10 Nov 2026). Xbox says the same for the Microsoft Store.
• Trailer 1: 90,421,491 YouTube views in its first 24 hours (Guinness World Records)

OUR MATH
• 17 Sept 2013 to 19 Nov 2026 = 4,811 days
• 90,421,491 views / 86,400 seconds ≈ 1,046 views every second
• Years between North American launches: III to Vice City ≈ 1, Vice City to San Andreas ≈ 2, San Andreas to IV ≈ 3.5, IV to V ≈ 5.4, V to VI ≈ 13.2

How old were you when GTA 5 came out? 👇

Follow for tomorrow. See you in Leonida.

Not affiliated with Rockstar Games or Take Two. Footage and images: Rockstar Games (official trailers, gameplay clips and screenshots). Narration is my own voice, AI assisted.
